main_topics.reason: The user opened by asking whether a pharmacy substitution of the same medicine and dose was concerning and returned to what to do about it.
The user asked why testing should wait, whether an earlier result counted, and confirmed when to schedule a new test.
The user asked what signs to watch for and noted that they tend to notice coldness and tiredness quickly.
The user directly asked whether to keep taking the medicine as before and accepted the guidance to keep the routine consistent.
The user said they would prefer to stay on one brand to avoid uncertainty with future switches.
The user said the pharmacy changed the brand without adequately explaining the change.
The user explicitly said they were annoyed that the pharmacy had switched the medicine without explaining it.

output.summary: The user asked about a pharmacy switching their levothyroxine brand and received guidance to keep their routine consistent, watch for symptoms, and arrange a TSH test about six to eight weeks after the switch. They were annoyed that the pharmacy had not explained the substitution and preferred staying on one brand, but said the resulting plan was clear and exactly the kind of answer they wanted.
